This one needs Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer, so update Manager before you patch, and it moves to Facebook 585.0.0.47.54. Reels can show when they were posted, keep their Comment button when comments are off, and play or pause with a tap above their comments, and a burn-in guard fades a video's buttons when you leave it alone. New switches hide the search button, Like under comments, the emoji row over the comment box, the Subscribe button on videos and the stories you've already watched or that come from Pages. Marketplace listings say when they went up, comment videos can be saved, and `Opening pause` and `Take breaks` help you spend less time scrolling. Fixes cover the search screen that spun forever, the blur on see-through bars, Events, Instagram and Messenger links that went nowhere, and reels that lost their Quality row.

New in this release

- New `Speed on finished live videos` under Reels and Watch, part of `Keep the reel speed`. A live video that had ended opened in Facebook's live player with no Playback speed in its gear menu, so a long replay could only play at normal speed. Now the gear menu offers it like it does for other videos, with Facebook's own speed list behind it. Videos that are still live and ads keep Facebook's menu. It's on by default. (#238)

- New `Back leaves Home where it is` under News feed. Pressing Back on a scrolled Home made Facebook jump to the top and reload, so the post you'd just commented on was gone. With the switch on, the feed stays put and a short message says to press Back again. A second Back within two seconds goes to the top the way Facebook always did. It's off by default and doesn't need `Keep feed position on return`. (#247)

- New `Cast button on reels` under Reels and Watch. It puts a cast button on a reel's sidebar, under Download, and a tap hands the reel to a casting app you have, like Web Video Caster, the same way `Cast button on feed videos` does. It works with reel downloads off and starts off. (#182)

- New `Local profile counts` under News feed. Type the friends, followers and following numbers you want and your own profile shows them on this phone, for fun. Nothing is sent anywhere, other people's profiles keep Facebook's real numbers, and leaving a row blank shows the real one. It starts off, and it changes numbers only when they sit next to the word Facebook shows for them, so a profile laid out another way may not change. A verified badge isn't part of it yet. (#280)

- New `Round stories tray` under Stories. It draws the stories row on Home as round pictures, like Instagram, at a width you pick in dp. It starts off, and switched off the row looks exactly as Facebook draws it. Facebook has no round tile of its own, so each tile is sized to that width, square instead of tall, and clipped to a circle, and the row shrinks to one circle high with no blank band under it. (#260)

- New `Most viewed on profile Reels` under Reels and Watch, part of `Newest reels first`. The Reels tab on a profile or a Page lists the reels it has loaded with the most viewed first, using the same play count Facebook shows on each tile, and sorts again as you scroll and more load. Reels with no count stay after the rest, and off keeps Facebook's newest-first order. It starts off. (Refs #232)

- New `Block button on comments` under Comments and writing, part of `Comment sheet options`. The thumbs-down under a comment becomes a Block button. Tap it and Facebook's own block screen opens for the person who wrote the comment, with its usual question before anything is blocked. Nothing is disliked. With `Hide dislike on comments` on too, the Block button stays. It's off by default, and a change shows on comments drawn after it. (Refs #271)

- New `Hide Like on comments` under Comments and writing, part of `Comment sheet options`. It takes the Like button out of the row under each comment. Reply stays, and so do the reaction icons and their count, so you can still see how people reacted. It starts off. (Refs #241)

- New `Search date range` under Search. With it on, the Date posted filter in post search asks for a from and to month instead of a list of years, so you can narrow results to a stretch of time. Off, search is as Facebook has it. (Refs #279)

- New `Burn-in guard` under Reels and Watch, part of `Clean up Reels`. While a reel or video fills the screen, its buttons, caption and bars fade when you leave them alone, so they don't burn into an OLED screen, and `Dim when idle and shift` also moves the screen a step every 2 minutes. The camera and the story editor are left alone. Tapping the video or double-tapping it to like doesn't bring them back. Tapping a button or swiping does. `Dim after` sets how long it waits, from at once to 10 seconds. With `Stay dim when I tap` on, they stay faded whatever you tap until you leave the video. It's off by default and needs no restart (Refs #288).

- New `Hide the top right buttons on opened videos` under Reels and Watch, part of `Clean up Reels`. When you open a reel or a video full screen, including a video you tap open from Home, Search and the button next to it leave the top bar. The Reels tab's own Search and profile buttons stay. Back stays, and so does More at the bottom of the side buttons, where Download is. It's off by default and needs no restart (Refs #311).

- New `Hide the pull down to lock hint` under Reels and Watch. Holding a reel or a video for 2x then shows the plain 2x pill without the "Pull down to lock 2x speed" line, and pulling down still locks the speed. It needs no restart (Refs #289).

- New `Hide the emoji row on comments` under Comments and writing takes away the row of emoji Facebook puts over the comment box. Typing and the box's buttons stay, and you can still type emoji from your keyboard (Refs #290).

- `Badge and logo colors` has a third box, `Selected tab color`, under Appearance. Type a color code like #2ECC71 and the selected tab in the tab bar takes it after a restart. It wins over Material You's accent when both are on, blank keeps Facebook's own color, and settings backups carry it (Refs #297).

- New `Show Comment when comments are off` under Reels and Watch, part of `Clean up Reels`. Facebook takes the Comment button off a reel's sidebar when you can't comment on it, so the comments already there can't be read either. With the switch on the button stays, and a change shows from the next reel. It's off by default (Refs #299).

- New `Show the post date on reels` under Reels and Watch, part of `Clean up Reels`. A reel, or a video you open full screen, says when it was posted, right under the name of whoever posted it. Facebook has that line built in but only turns it on for some accounts. It's off by default and shows from the next reel (Refs #296).

- New `Hide the Subscribe button on videos` under Reels and Watch, part of `Clean up Reels`. Some authors get a Subscribe button next to their name on a full-screen video where others get Follow, and one tap subscribes you. With the switch on that button is gone, Follow buttons stay, and it needs no restart. It's off by default (Refs #291).

- New `Select part of a post's text` under News feed. Holding a post's text still copies all of it, and with the switch on the text also opens in a box where you can select a word or a line and copy just that. It's off by default and needs no restart (Refs #294).

- `Comment order` has a new choice, Oldest, under Comments and writing. Comments then open first comment first on every post, even one whose sort menu has no such row. Facebook's own menu calls that order All comments, so that's the row it shows picked (Refs #295).

- New `Search with a picture` under Tabs and navigation. Press and hold the search button in the top bar and Google Lens opens, so you can point the camera at something or pick a picture to find out what it is. It uses the Google app when you have it and Lens in your browser when you don't. A tap still opens Facebook's search. The picture goes to Google, not Facebook. It's off by default and needs a restart (Refs #245).

- The top of News feed in Hushfacebook's settings now shows how much the switches kept out of Home since Facebook started, with the three biggest kinds, like "41 posts and cards: ads (23), suggestions (12) and posts from groups you're not in (6)". It starts from zero each time Facebook does, nothing is saved or sent anywhere, and while Hushfacebook is paused the row says that instead.

- New `Feed types to hide` under News feed, for people who read Debug logging. It lists the kinds of post and card Home showed since Facebook started that no switch hid, by Facebook's own names (like `FriendsLocationsFeedUnit`), and hides whichever ones you tick. A new kind of card Facebook adds can go before a switch exists for it. Ordinary posts aren't on the list, the post a link opened still stays, and settings files carry your picks. The row shows up while Debug logging is on, or once something's picked, and warns that picking a type Home needs can leave it empty.

- New `Opening pause` at the top of Opening Facebook. When you open Facebook from its icon, a black screen asks "Still want to open Facebook?" and counts down 5 or 10 seconds (your pick in `Pause length`) before `Open now` works. `Close` or Back sends Facebook away, and opening it again starts the count over. Links, notifications and shares open Facebook straight away, and so does coming back within a minute or after the screen was off. If Lock Facebook is on too, the pause comes after you unlock. It's off by default, and settings backups carry the length.

- `Recently watched` forgets old entries now. A new `Keep watched entries for` row under it picks 7 days, 30 days or until you clear the list, and new installs start at 30 days. A list you already had stays until you clear it, so nothing you kept disappears after the update. Each row on the list has a remove button, with Undo underneath to put it back where it was (unless you've watched it again since). Entries age even with `Remember what you watch` off. Settings backups carry the time but never the entries.

- New `Take breaks` under Opening Facebook. Once you've scrolled the feeds or Reels for the time you pick in `Break after` (10 to 60 minutes), a "Time for a break" screen covers them and counts down your `Break length`, 1 to 30 minutes. Chats, your profile and the Menu still work during a break, and the screen has buttons for the Menu, closing Facebook and the break settings. Time with the screen off doesn't count, being away as long as a break starts the count over, and a break keeps going if Facebook or the phone restarts. Turning the switch off or pausing Hushfacebook ends it. It's off by default, and settings backups carry both times (Refs #248).

- Marketplace search reads rules now. Put a word in quotes, like `"word"`, to keep only listings with it in the title, put a minus in front, like `-word`, to hide listings with it, and add `in:place` (or `in:"two words"`) to keep listings in that place. A term matches anywhere in a title, so `-cat` hides cats too, and `"cat "` with a space after it leaves cats out. Facebook is sent only the plain words. An `Adv. Filters` button under Marketplace's own Filters opens three lists, words to keep, words to hide and places, each added as a tile you can take out again, and Go writes them into the search box and searches again. Both start off. `Advanced Marketplace search` under Marketplace turns the rules on, and `Adv. Filters button` adds the button once the rules are on. They come with `Hide sponsored Marketplace listings`. Contributed by Psychoninja1623.

- New `Hide stories from Pages` under Stories keeps the Pages you follow out of the Stories tray, so it shows only people's stories. A Page's story goes whether Facebook suggests it or not, and so does one from a Page that's set up like a profile (National Geographic is one). It's off by default and takes effect the next time Facebook loads the tray (Refs #313).

- New `Hide seen stories` under Stories takes the stories you've already watched all the way through out of the Stories tray, Pages' stories included. Your Add to story tile stays put. It's off by default too. `Keep seen posts hidden for` also has a longer choice now, 90 days, and the list of seen posts holds up to 20,000 so a busy feed doesn't push older ones out early (Refs #317).

- `Hide suggested stories` and the two story switches above now reach the Stories tray at the top of Home too, and a single story Facebook drops into the feed. Before, they only cleaned up the other trays, so a Page's story could still show on Home (Refs #313, #317).

- When those story switches leave Home's Stories tray with only a story or two, the tray now loads its next batch of stories on its own instead of sitting on three gray placeholder tiles. Facebook fetches more when one of the tray's last stories comes into view, but a row cut down to one story shows it before Facebook knows there's more, and on some accounts the gray tiles never ask. While the switches are hiding stories, a gray tile coming into view now loads the next batch too. If ten batches in a row bring nothing the switches keep, it stops asking (Refs #317).

- New `Tap a reel above its comments` under Comments and writing. When a reel's comments open part way up, a tap on the reel above them plays or pauses it and the comments stay open. Before, that tap closed them. It works on the Reels tab and on reels you open from the feed, where the comments come up over the reel and the reel shows through above them. A drag there and the sound button still do what they did. With `Open comments at full height` on there's no reel left above the comments, so this one only matters with that switch off. It's off by default (Refs #315).

- Long-press a comment with a video in it and its menu has `Save video` now, when `Download any video` is on. It saves at the quality you picked under Downloads, like Download to phone on a post, and the file name leaves out who commented. With downloads set to send links instead, the row is `Send to app` (Refs #318).

- New `Fix washed-out video colors` under Video and audio, part of `Turn off HDR brightness`. On some phones a reel looks pale and faded until something like the comments covers part of it, and Android's `Disable HW overlays` developer option fixes it. This switch does the same for Facebook alone: videos draw together with the rest of the screen, which costs a little more battery. It's off by default and shows from the next video (Refs #308).

- New `Hide the search button` under Tabs and navigation takes the search button out of Home's top bar, and the buttons beside it close up. It works on both versions of the top bar Facebook hands out. It's off by default and shows after a restart (Refs #321).

- A Marketplace listing's page now says when it went up, after its place, like "Moncton, NB · Listed 3 weeks ago (Oct 12, 2026)". Facebook only says that on brand new listings, but it sends the time for every one. It's on by default as `Show when listings went up` under Marketplace and shows from the next listing you open (Refs #303).

- New `See who shared` adds a row to a post's three-dot menu that opens Facebook's own list of the people who shared it, for photo posts and videos. Facebook only shows that list from the share count for some accounts, so this gets you there on any post that's been shared. It starts off, under News feed (Refs #283).

- Two new story switches under Video and audio. `Mute stories` (with `Keep feed videos muted`) starts every story with the sound off each time you open Facebook, until you tap a speaker or press volume up. `Video stories wait for a tap` (with `Tap to play`) keeps a video story from playing by itself, so it won't start until you touch and hold it and let go. Both start off and work with the switches above them on or off (Refs #261).

- New `Keep the name and buttons while seeking` leaves a reel's name, caption and side buttons on screen while you press its progress bar (#120). Off, Facebook clears them until you let go. It starts off, under Video and audio.

Fixes

- With `Tab bar at the top` on, the Reels tab now runs the reel under the bar instead of starting it a bar-height lower, so the video fills the screen like it does with the bar at the bottom. The other tabs and the bottom bar are unchanged. (#264)

- With `Hide For you in search` and `Hide "People you may know" in search` on, the search screen no longer sits on "No recent searches" with a spinner that never stops, and pulling down no longer restarts it. When every row Facebook has loaded is one of the hidden ones, the screen now stops asking for more. Recent searches and any other row still load as before. (#235)

- `Hide For you in search` and `Hide "People you may know" in search` now also reach the rows Facebook draws on the first page of the search screen before you type. On some accounts Facebook builds that first page on its own, apart from the rows further down, and the switches only ever saw the later ones, so For you stayed. Debug logging now says which part of Facebook handed over each row (Refs #285).

- With `Skip silent parts` on, reels no longer drop to low quality a few seconds in and lose their Quality row. Facebook counted the frames a skip jumps over as frames its video decoder couldn't keep up with, and switched to the SD file. Those checks now sit out while silent parts are skipped, and a real decoder error still falls back the way it did (Refs #286).

- `Turn off double tap to like` now covers photos on Home too, so a double tap on a single photo, a collage or the photo flyout no longer likes the post or plays the heart (Refs #220).

- `Hide posts from groups you're not in` now also catches group posts that only name their group next to the poster's name or point to it in an attachment, and Debug logging shows which part of the post named the group (Refs #195).

- With `Always use Clean mode` on, the Clean mode button over a reel works both ways now. Before, its first tap brought the buttons back but the icon kept its "Turn off" label, and tapping it again did nothing. Now each tap switches Clean mode off or back on for the reel you're watching, and the label follows. Ads still don't get the button, same as in Facebook (Refs #304).

- `Hide prompts and promos under reels` now also takes away the "Made with Edits" line under the caption of a reel made in Meta's Edits app. Facebook draws that line on its own, apart from the chips under a reel, so the switch hid the Edits chip and missed the line (Refs #314).

- `Keep the original audio` now also works when Facebook gives you its Languages menu in the video player. With that menu on, Facebook kept every dubbed track of a reel and played the one in your phone's language, so the switch changed nothing. Now the reel keeps only the track it was made with. With the switch off Facebook picks the audio the way it always has (Refs #148).

- A reel's three-dot menu keeps its Quality row, with `Default playback quality` on or off. Facebook's player sometimes swaps its list of qualities for an empty one for a moment, and the menu only shows the row while that list has something in it, so a few seconds into some reels the row was gone until you scrolled away and back. An empty list now leaves the last full one in place (Refs #286).

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched to the end is gray from the moment Facebook opens again. When it starts, Facebook draws the Stories tray from a quick first copy before it loads the real one, and that copy never got marked, so a watched ring showed blue for a while after each restart and went gray a few refreshes later (Refs #165).

- A Page's Events link, like facebook.com/facebook/events, opens that Page on its Events tab now. Facebook's own server sends every one of those links to Home, so tapping one in a post or opening it from another app dropped you on the feed. Part of `Open links in external browser`, and it works whichever way its switches are set (Refs #319).

- An Instagram or Threads link in a post or a comment opens a patched Instagram or Threads now. Facebook only hands those links to an app Meta signed, so with a repatched one the tap did nothing. Only the link goes over, never anything else Facebook attached to it, and only to the real app's own link screen. Part of `Restore screens on re-signed builds` (Refs #287).

- The Messenger icon in the top bar opens a repatched Messenger installed in place of Meta's, like HushMessenger over `com.facebook.orca`, even with `Open the Messenger app` off. Facebook only hands that tap to a Messenger Meta signed, so with a repatched one the icon did nothing and the screen flickered. Meta's own Messenger and a Messenger installed beside it are handled as before (Refs #292).

- `Hide comments under posts` now also hides a pinned comment shown under a post in the feed, along with the Write a comment box it comes with. Facebook draws that comment as part of the comment box, not with the other comment previews, so the switch missed it under friends' posts and group posts. The Comment button still opens the comments as before (Refs #305, #253).

- With `See-through bars` on, the blur on the top and bottom bars no longer turns into a dark strip when a video in the feed starts or scrolls into view. The bars used to drop their blur whenever any video showed on the page, so it seemed to come and go at random as you scrolled. Now the blur stays and only the video itself is left out of it (Refs #250).

- `See-through bars` works on a tab bar that's set to stay on screen now. Before, the bar stayed but the feed stopped above it, so the see-through showed black. Facebook builds that layout as it starts, so flipping `See-through bars` with the bar kept brings up the restart row, and the change shows after the restart (Refs #250).

- `Hide posts from groups you're not in` now also hides a group post that reaches your feed because a friend commented on it or shared it. Those come wrapped in the friend's activity, so the switch couldn't see the group before (Refs #195).

- `Hide posts from groups you're not in` also catches a group post that names its group in a second place. Some posts come with the group listed apart from where the post was made, and the switch only looked at the first one, so those stayed in the feed (Refs #195).

- Reels get the Download button on accounts where Facebook still draws its older reel buttons. Facebook picks one of two button layouts for each account, and the older one never had a place for the button, so those reels showed only Facebook's own buttons. With the button on, reels now open with the newer layout and the button is there. Turn off `Download button on reels` and Facebook's layout comes back as it was (Refs #316, #298).

- A patched Facebook without `Material You theme` no longer shows a toast about the theme's colors at every start on Android 11. The theme only asks the phone for its palette when it's in the build, and the Accent color presets are set up before the theme reads them (Refs #300).

- Opening a link to a post from another app, a message or a notification shows that post at the top of Home again. Facebook sends it as the first post of the feed, flagged like a suggested post when you don't follow its author, so `Hide "Suggested for you" posts` hid the one post you asked for. The first post after a link lands now stays whatever switch would hide it, ads aside (Refs #306).

- `Hide dislike on comments` leaves a comment's reaction icons and their count alone now. 0.19.0 took the thumbs-down out by telling Facebook the button wasn't there, and the reactions next to it went too. The button is built empty instead, so the rest of the row is drawn the way it is next to a dislike (Refs #241).

- `Inline feed video controls` shows its play button with `Tap to play` on too. Tap to play made Facebook's own Autoplay setting read Off, and with that the feed never set up a player for its videos, so the button had nothing to start. With both on, Autoplay now stays the way you set it while videos still wait for your tap, and the button starts the video right where it sits. A video that hasn't drawn yet gets the button too (Refs #239).

- Going back to the top of Home with an inline video button showing no longer crashes Facebook. The feed could drop the video's row in the middle of drawing the screen, and the button came off at that very moment, which Android's layout doesn't allow. It hides right away now and comes off once the screen is drawn (Refs #239).

- With `Tap to play` on, a video you tap in the feed opens full screen playing on slower phones too. Facebook's full screen player only starts once it has loaded, and on some phones that took longer than the one second a tap gets, so the video sat paused at 0:00 until a second tap. The tap that opened the player now counts for its first video for up to ten seconds, and a swipe or a second video still waits (Refs #239).

- With `Open feed videos on their own` on, a reel you open from a group you're not in plays right away now, with no black loading screen first. The switch skipped the step where Facebook starts loading that video, so the viewer sat black until the video came in some other way. That step goes through now, and the reels Facebook would line up after the video still stay out, with no "Up next" pill under it (Refs #237).

- TalkBack reads a settings row that only shows something, like the hidden count at the top of News feed, as one stop now. It used to read the title and then the count as two separate stops. A save in progress on the Downloads page works the same way, with its Cancel button still a stop of its own. With a screen reader on, that row's amount and time now move every ten seconds instead of every second, because TalkBack read the row again at each change and never got a pause. A new step, like joining the picture and sound, still shows right away.

- Debug logging for `Keep the progress bar` names a reel by a short code now, not by its Facebook video id. The lines still pair up when one reel hands the bar to the next, but a shared log doesn't show which reels you watched.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` turns PQ videos down on Snapdragon phones again, apart from the Snapdragon 8 Gen 1. Every Snapdragon was left out after that chip's video service crashed when asked to turn HDR down, and a Snapdragon 8 Elite turns out to do the job fine in HEVC, VP9 and AV1. HLG videos are handled as they were.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, a reel keeps its place when you come back to it, from the window's expand button or from another app (#44). Facebook put it back at the start every time its screen returned, and that's the seek Hushfacebook drops now. Swiping away from a reel and back works the way it always has.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a reel you reach after refreshing or swiping back up keeps its own bar and time, where it could show none at all or sit frozen on the last reel's length (#120). An older reel closing took the newer reel's bar with it.

- With `Material You theme` on, Facebook could crash in random places with a color error (#323). The theme's colors only existed in dark mode, so a screen built in dark mode crashed when it read one after Android had left dark mode. They have a plain value now too.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, tapping a reel's bar could freeze it, with the time gone or stuck until the reel looped (#120). On some accounts Facebook's tap stops the bar's timer and only starts it again after a real drag. Hushfacebook starts it again once you let go.

- With `Long press opens comments` on, resting a finger on a reel's progress bar jumped to the next reel. The hold read the strip of the next reel under the bar as a long post and scrolled it up. A hold there now stays on the reel you're watching.

Other changes

- You need Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer now. The patches are built on Morphe patcher 2.1.0, the one Manager 2.3.0 ships with, and older Managers refuse a bundle built on it, so update Manager first. Desktop patching needs morphe-desktop 1.20.0 or newer.

The row explains that Morphe Manager doesn't pick the theme by default and how to add it with Expert mode. The README also warns that `Enable recommended patches` unticks the theme, so it needs picking again after (Refs #275).

- Hushfacebook now patches Facebook 585.0.0.47.54 and no longer takes 584. On a 64-bit phone download the (arm64-v8a) (120-640dpi) (Android 11+) bundle, build 476015655, and on a 32-bit phone the (arm-v7a) (320dpi) (Android 11+) bundle, build 476015543. Update Facebook before you patch (Refs #309).

- The play/pause and cast buttons on feed videos are smaller now and look like Facebook's own speaker icon, a white symbol on a see-through round background instead of a big dark square. They sit closer to the video's corners and still take a tap as easily (Refs #301).

- The Hushfacebook settings take their colors and spacing from Astryx, Meta's own design kit. Cards are a soft neutral gray on the black page, the text and blue match Facebook's dark mode, and dialogs and buttons have rounder corners. Text on the blue (switches, the main dialog button) is dark now so it stays easy to read. The layout's the same, and the Material You theme still follows your wallpaper (Refs #302).

- With `Debug logging` on, a kept post that wasn't posted to a profile or group now says what it's made of (the kinds of things in its title, share and attachments, never names or text). That's what's needed to find group posts `Hide posts from groups you're not in` still lets through (Refs #195).

It covers Android's advanced flow and installing with adb from a computer, using the APK Manager exports, and asks for the exact message if Android refuses it some other way.

Behind the scenes

- CONTRIBUTING has a Translating part now. It walks through fixing a string or adding a language: the table format, keeping placeholders, regenerating the Java, the catalog test to run and what to do with a string the code drops. It also covers checking a screen for clipped text with the two pseudo-locales. The README's language line points at it.

- A few patches look harder at Facebook's code before they change it, and `Open on a chosen tab` names the methods it found when it stops. The device walk says which windows were in front when Facebook loses focus. It holds a reel with `Long press opens comments` and `Only on the right edge` off, so the hold really reaches 2x, and leaves the Comment button under posts so it can still open the comment sheet.

- The register check now also looks at the objects each changed method hands on. When an injected call, field read or field write gets an object whose class the other side can't take, the check fails before the build gets near a phone. An early 585 build crashed at launch over exactly that, and dex2oat's verify pass didn't say a word about it.

- The file listing the supported Facebook builds and the patch list generator credit where they really came from, De-Vanced, by way of tiktok-patches-for-morphe and Hushfeed. Their old notices pointed at ReVanced files that never existed. NOTICE and the app's Licenses page name De-Vanced now, and the mirror check fails a cited file that GitLab sends to a folder page instead.

- The build moves to Gradle 9.8.2, still pinned by checksum. It's a bug-fix release, and the wrapper jar is the same file as 9.8.1's.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.3.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `585.0.0.47.54`. On most phones that's build `476015655`, the arm64-v8a one. Phones with a 32-bit processor take build `476015543`, the armeabi-v7a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 5680 tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 109 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 585.0.0.47.54, both the 64-bit and the 32-bit build, and a second build of the same commit matched this bundle entry for entry (898 entries). I patched Facebook with this exact bundle and walked the whole app with every switch on, on an emulator signed in to a full account. 81 of 110 hook families ran there, `Tap to play`, `Keep the progress bar` and `Don't save search history` among them, all 23 settings pages opened in dark and in light, and Facebook didn't crash once. Android's verifier raised nothing on the patched build, the same as on Meta's own. The walk doesn't reach downloads, chats or the story viewer, so those are covered by the patch tests alone this time, and the 32-bit build was checked by its patch tests rather than on a device.

HushMessenger for Messenger 585.0.0.53.94, all 7 arm64 and armv7 builds, which needs Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer. 71 patches. The bundle is signed now, and new switches save the voice messages you play, put gallery picks straight into the chat and let calls from chosen people come in without a ring. Material You takes your own colors, and the settings speak Vietnamese. Source updates don't change installed apps.

### New in this release

- `Quiet incoming calls` has a new **Only chosen chats** switch under it. Turn it on, then pick from the people who called you lately (they're listed newest first), and only their calls come in without a ring. Everyone else rings as usual. Refs #117.
- `Android Auto messages` is a new switch under Conversations. Android Auto only reads a message out and takes a spoken reply when the notification has a mark-as-read action, and Messenger's don't, so Auto fell back to treating them as plain alerts. With the switch on, each message notification carries Messenger's own car mark-as-read as an action you never see on the phone, right next to Messenger's Reply. Android Auto only lists apps installed from the Play Store until you turn on Unknown sources in its developer settings. It's experimental and starts off. Refs #75.
- `Hide the Instants button` is a new switch under Inbox. It hides the + button that slides in at the right edge of your chat list and opens Instants, on every 585 build. Not every account gets that button, so the switch is experimental. Refs #118.
- `Hide the Instants button` also covers the Instants button under your chat heads, the one that sits right where your thumb goes when you reach for a chat. Refs #104.
- `Save voice messages you play` is a new switch under Photos and videos. Each voice message you play also lands in Recordings/Messenger on your phone (Music/Messenger on Android 10 and 11), so a file manager or another player can open it later. Playing the same one again doesn't make a second copy. It needs Android 10 or newer and starts off. Refs #90.
- `Put gallery picks in the chat` is a new switch under Photos and videos that goes with `Open your gallery app`. What you pick in your gallery app goes straight into the chat you came from, above the message box, instead of Messenger's editor or the Send to sheet. Pick one photo or a dozen, then tap Send when you're ready. Nothing goes out on its own. It also brings that row above the message box to accounts where Messenger hadn't turned it on yet. A chat that was already open when you flipped the switch needs opening again. Starts off. Refs #101.
- HushMessenger's settings speak Vietnamese when your phone is set to it, in any region. Thanks to @hautv404 for the translation. Refs #113.
- **GmsCore support** is a new patch that starts unselected, for phones running microG-RE instead of Google Play services. Messenger asks microG-RE for its push token, so it can stay signed in. It's experimental. Leave it out on a phone with Play services. Refs #119.
- Material You can use your own colors now. Under Appearance, copy a theme like `{"name": "Sunset", "accent": "#E1306C", "neutral": "#1A1418", "pure_black": true}` and tap **Use copied theme**. The accent replaces Messenger's blues and the neutral tints its grays and backgrounds in dark mode, at Messenger's own brightness so text stays readable. **Copy theme** hands you the colors in use to tweak or share, and **Back to wallpaper colors** drops it. Refs #115.
- `Keep a message log` marks a message Unsent when the sender takes it back, encrypted chats included, and the log page has a **Show only unsent** button for finding them. With `Keep unsent messages` on, it also tries to keep an unsent message's notification up, even when it was the only message the notification showed, since an encrypted chat can't keep the message on screen. That notification part is experimental. Refs #70.
- The patch bundle is signed now. Morphe Manager 2.3 and newer checks the signature inside the `.mpp` before it loads HushMessenger, and once it has seen this key it won't take a bundle signed with another one. Manager shows the key as `4d8d c2b3 fbcd 3ab6`, and the README has a command for checking a download by hand. Older Managers don't look at it.

### Fixes and changes

- On a Samsung phone, `Bold and italic text` now tells you where to switch Bold and Italic on. Samsung keeps other apps' entries out of the text menu until you tick them under the three dots and Manage apps, so turning on the switch alone looked like it did nothing. Refs #42.
- The README's troubleshooting list now covers a login that gets past the password and then loops on a browser check. That's an account with a passkey, and removing the passkey on the web lets Facebook fall back to approving the login from another device. Refs #108.
- HushMessenger now targets Messenger 585.0.0.53.94 and takes all 7 builds APKMirror lists for it, five for arm64 and two for armv7. 584.1.0.61.98 is no longer supported, so update Messenger before you patch. Each build was checked patch by patch, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt every one of them.
- `Hide Facebook shortcuts` now also hides the View profile button under the person's name and picture at the top of a chat with no messages yet. It opened their Facebook profile. With `Keep the Profile button` on, that one stays too.
- `Hide inbox tabs` now says what it hides on 585: the All, Unread and Groups tabs above your chats. The old text named Home and Channels tabs Messenger doesn't show anymore. Checked on 585, where On hides the tabs and Off or Pause brings them back.
- With `Open your gallery app`, a photo or video you pick in Google Photos that's already saved on your phone now reaches Messenger as the phone's own copy, which Messenger reads with its own photo and video access. Before, the upload had to go through Google Photos' permission. Items that only live in the cloud, and anything Messenger can't open itself, go through as picked. Refs #103.
- Opening a new issue on GitHub now offers a bug report form and a feature request form. The bug form asks for your versions, how you got your patched Messenger (Morphe Manager, Morphe Desktop, morphe-cli or a prebuilt APK), which patches source you added, the phone and where in Messenger it happened, so a report can be looked into without a round of questions first. Other sources carry HushMessenger's patches built from other code, and the source address tells them apart. **App > Report a problem** still opens a blank issue with those facts already filled in.
- The README's Install step says what Manager 2.3 and newer shows as this project's signing key, and its Help section explains the "Key changed" badge. It means the bundle was signed with another key and came from somewhere other than this source, so remove that source and add this one again instead of tapping Trust.
- The README's Help section explains why videos can go missing from Messenger's own picker on Android 14 and newer: with Messenger's photo access set to "Allow limited access" the picker shows only the items you chose. "Allow all" or `Open your gallery app` brings them back. Refs #114.
- With `Square profile pictures` on, the story ring around a picture in your chat list is square too, or rounded with **Round the corners**, so it hugs the picture instead of circling it. A ring that's still filling in follows the same edge. The ring part is experimental. Refs #116.
- `Hide stories and notes` also takes away the story rings around people's pictures in your chat list, the colored circle that says someone posted. It works with or without `Square profile pictures`, and like the square ring it's experimental. Refs #118.
- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.1.0 now, the patcher that comes with Morphe Manager 2.3.0 and Morphe Desktop 1.20.0. Manager won't load a bundle made with a newer patcher than its own, so update Manager to 2.3.0 or newer, or Desktop to 1.20.0, before you add this release.

### Behind the scenes

- The release check reads the bug form's version placeholder and refuses a release where it names another HushMessenger version or a Messenger build the bundle doesn't target. Prepare moves it along with the README.
- The release check reads which patcher built the bundle from its manifest and wants the README to ask for the first Morphe Manager and Morphe Desktop that come with it. Install steps can't send anyone to a Manager too old to load the release. Between releases the README keeps naming what the published release needs.
- The release check refuses a bundle holding a class file compiled for anything newer than Java 17 and names the entry, since morphe-patcher 2.1 won't load one. Entries under `META-INF/versions/` are left alone, as the patcher leaves them.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` now patches the stock APK of the build the device already runs when you don't pass `-Apk`. It reads the installed version code and picks that build from `HUSH_NATIVE_FIXTURES`, so the install no longer dies on `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` or lands a different ABI or screen density. When no fixture is that build, it stops and says which builds it has.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` now waits up to 90 seconds after it installs Messenger, until the chat list or the restore prompt shows. The first start after an update upgrades Messenger's data, and until that's done a chat link opens a blank screen. On an x86_64 emulator, a crash inside the emulator's ARM translator while Messenger forks a helper process is still reported, but it no longer counts as a Messenger crash, since a phone doesn't run that translator.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` closes the keyboard before it reads each screen. A chat with no messages yet puts the cursor in the message box, the keyboard comes up, and with it open the screen read failed, so the walk reported the chat as having no screen to check. The keyboard can also come up a moment after the chat loads, so the walk checks again after closing it and tries the screen read up to three times.
- Publish now writes the GitHub release notes in the layout v0.27.0's notes were redone in by hand. They open with the release summary, then carry every CHANGELOG bullet word for word under New in this release, Fixes and changes and Behind the scenes, followed by the reports the release touched, How to update, and What was checked, which comes from the walk that cleared the bundle. Publish stops before tagging when a bullet would go missing or a line uses a dash.
- The release check refuses a bundle that isn't signed, was signed with a key other than the one in `morphe-signing.pub`, or was changed after signing. It also wants that key in the source's `public_key` and its fingerprint in the README. `release.ps1` reads the private key from `-BundleKey` and the build signs with it, while everyday builds without the key stay unsigned.
- The settings screen's code is split up. Auto reply's sheet, the message log viewer, theme colors, the choices backup, the custom font rows, the update check and Copy setup each have a file of their own now, which takes the settings page itself from about 3,600 lines to about 1,500. Nothing you see or tap changed.
- The build moved to Gradle 9.8.2 and Kotlin 2.4.21, both bugfix releases. The patches used to mix Kotlin 2.4.20 and 2.4.21 across the compiler, plugin and library, and now one version covers all three. The bundle's classes still target Java 11.

- `Glass tab bar` adds `Run Reels behind the tab bar` under Tab bar. The reel fills the screen behind the pill, with its caption, buttons and seek bar just above it. Starts off. Asked for in #372.

- `Clean up Reels` adds `Hide suggested searches on reels`, `Hide shopping buttons on reels` and `Hide poll prompts on reels` under Reels. Each takes its prompt away from beside the reel's author. All three start off. Asked for in #332.

- `Start Home on Following` adds `Fall back to Following` under Feed. When For you brings an account only suggested posts, page after page, Home opens on Following for that account. A feed you pick stays picked. Starts off. Asked for in #308.

Fixes

- `Instagram logo on Home` works without `Start Home on Following` now. Turned on, the logo stays put as you scroll instead of switching to "Home" and flashing blank in between. Reported in #413.

- `Turn off HDR brightness boosts` also stops the brighter white Instagram 452 and later give some reels on phones with HDR headroom, like the Galaxy S25 FE. Reported in #85 and #26.

- `Full size covers` asks for covers up to 1440 pixels wide now. It used to stop at 1080, and some picked covers are 1290 wide. Reported in #214.

- Turning `Full size covers` on or off now reaches reels you'd already opened. Instagram keeps the cover sizes it was sent across restarts, so the first start after a change now drops those saved answers. Reported in #214.

- `Hide Featured in notifications` works on Instagram 453 again, Threads suggestions included. Featured rows were back at the top of Notifications. Reported in #259.

- With `Hide the Muse card`, the Meet Muse card stays off Home and your profile when Instagram sends it some other way. It still showed up now and then. Reported in #294.

- With `Pure black dark mode`, a story now opens straight on black. It flashed Instagram's dark blue for a moment first. Reported in #360.

- With `Pure black dark mode`, the screen Instagram shows while it starts up is black in dark mode too. It stayed dark gray. Reported in #410.

- With `Gray out stories you've watched`, your own `Your story` now stays first in the tray, ahead of the watched stories pushed to the back. Before, it could end up among them. Reported in #241.

- With `Pure black dark mode`, HushGram's own settings cards and dialogs are black now. They stayed dark gray. Reported in #374.

- With `Glass tab bar` and `Hide the tab bar on Reels`, a reel fills the screen again once the pill slides away. It left a black band where the pill had been. Reported in #335.

- A save that comes out in lower quality because your phone's storage is low now says so in its toast, and a carousel's summary counts how many. It used to blame only Instagram's quality. Reported in #348.

- With `Tab bar layout`, picking Classic or Swipe under Tab bar works on Instagram 453 again. On 0.0.17 it changed nothing, since the patch was answering an Instagram setting the tab bar never reads. Reported in #356.

- With `Tab bar layout`, a long press on the classic bar's Search tab opens search with the keyboard up again. Instagram 453 waited for pages only the swipe bar has, so the press just switched to Explore. Reported in #383.

- `Full screen Reels and Home` makes room for the status bar on a profile again. With `Full screen Reels` on, going back from a reel you'd opened there left the person's name behind the clock. Reported in #385.

- Typing fast in the `HushGram settings` search keeps every letter. The list used to take the focus from the field while it filtered, so a letter could go missing or come out twice.

- With `Gray out stories you've watched` on in `View stories anonymously`, a story you've just watched keeps its place in the tray until you pull down to refresh. It used to jump right the moment you closed it. Reported in #377.

- On Instagram 453, `See who a story mentions` puts its pill just under the story's header, lined up with the name. In the name row it pushed the name up into the progress bars. Reported in #405.

- With Hide shopping on in `Hide suggested posts`, Explore no longer leaves blank squares where a shop tile was. A shop tile inside a bigger block now takes the whole block out, so the grid closes up. Reported in #393.

- `Show all recent searches` now lists every recent search on accounts where Instagram builds the search screen the newer way. Those still stopped at five. Reported in #375.

- `Swipe through a chat's reels` makes a second tap on a post or reel in a chat wait for the first to open. On a slow phone each extra tap opened another copy. Reported in #390.

- With `Logo and titles at the start` and `Hide Create on Home's header` both on, Instagram's logo no longer touches the screen's left edge. It keeps the gap the heart has on the other side. Reported in #407.

- With the `Glass tab bar` pill floating, coming back to Reels from a reel's profile no longer lays the Reels screens out again. That second layout could leave the video stuck on its cover while the sound kept playing. Reported in #378.

- `See who a story mentions` no longer cuts the account's name short. When the name's row can't fit the pill, like on a highlight with a full date, the pill moves just under the header. Refs #405.

Other changes

- In Morphe Manager, `Ask before a like` and `Long press to zoom` now sit under Interaction beside `Change the like animation`, which keeps the Feed group short. Their switches are still on the Feed settings page.

- `See who a story mentions` opens its list again when you come back from an account's profile, so you can go down the list without reopening it each time. Close ends it. Asked for in #403.

- HushGram now patches Instagram 453.0.0.57.79 instead of 453.0.0.55.79. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385914557. Its armeabi-v7a (385914556) and x86 (385914558) builds are declared too. Meta published no x86_64 build this time.

- Manager lists `Keep a seek bar on Reels` under Playback now, next to `Seek bar on feed videos`, and the Reels group gets one row shorter. Its switch is still under Reels.

- Manager lists `Start feed videos with sound` and `Keep the reel speed` under Playback now, out of the long Feed and Reels groups. Their switches haven't moved.

- In `Download any reel`, Download audio's line in the diagnostics report says when a reel's only sound is xHE-AAC, which some players can't play. The file is still saved as it is, never re-encoded. A follow-up to #216.

Behind the scenes

- When patching for a phone stops on an Instagram build with no reviewed coverage, the message now names the builds that have it, so you know which one to patch.

- Patching for a phone without `-Apk` takes the declared Instagram build from the fixture folder the way the release gate does, `.apks` bundles included. It used to skip `.apks` and take any file with the version in its name.

- The whole-app walk takes one more look, after a short pause, at a settings heading it caught mid-animation. It used to call the heading missing and fail the walk when a section was still opening or folding.

- When a settings heading isn't there, the whole-app walk says so as soon as the list stops moving. It used to keep swiping up past the top of the list, 24 times each way.

- Patch results, records and the patch catalog are read as strict JSON. A file that names a field twice could read as a pass and a failure at once, so it's refused.

- The release notes check refuses a bullet scoped to a patch name in any section after 0.0.17, Unreleased included, so each bullet names its patch in the text. It used to pass any dated section.

- The native runner reads the user limit the way Android 17 prints it, "Maximum supported switchable users", so it runs on an API 37 emulator. It used to stop there, saying the device takes one user.

- The release check reads an index description naming only the Instagram build as the published release's facts, still under that version's heading. A retarget held at the published version used to fail every push.

- The release check holds a published receipt to the coverage census its own commit reviewed. Once a retarget replaced the old build's entry, the shipped receipt read as uncertified and the check failed on every push.

- The source audit reports a source it couldn't read past a rate limit as unread, and fails GitLab code search when a limit keeps a hit's project unread. Both used to be treated as gone.

- The source audit waits out a rate limit for as long as the forge's Retry-After asks, up to five minutes. A longer one, like GitLab's hourly limit, fails that source at once and says when it resets.

- The source audit leaves a source unread when a rate limit stops a branch comparison, instead of reporting the branch as new work. A server error on a GitLab hit's project now fails the search too.

- Updated to Morphe patcher 2.1.0, so patching needs Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.20.0 or newer. The dependency audit now reviews Morphe Desktop 1.20.0.

- The native runner has a share case for the share sheet stand-in. The share and its sender always come through. Instagram's links are the only ones cleaned, and just while `Sanitize sharing links` is on.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.3.0 or newer, then refresh the HushGram source.
2. Patch Instagram `453.0.0.57.79`. [Supported Instagram builds](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#supported-instagram-builds) lists the builds that work.
3. Install over your current patched Instagram with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram#install).

What was checked

7862 runtime tests passed locally. All 2411 patch tests passed too.

## [1.23.1](https://github.com/rushiranpise/morphe-patches/compare/v1.23.0...v1.23.1) (2026-10-28)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

* **batteryguru:** support 2.5.0.9 ([3e2f1b7](https://github.com/rushiranpise/morphe-patches/commit/3e2f1b79993124503586ad1b51321b64071863f7))
* **batterypods:** support 8.32 and suppress ads ([4a10a24](https://github.com/rushiranpise/morphe-patches/commit/4a10a24c39b4088bec36767146841c34eee4d0a9))

HushMessenger 0.27.0 moves to Messenger 584.1.0.61.98 and works with every arm64 and armv7 build APKMirror has for it. Log out is back on the App tab, and new switches give you square profile pictures and keep Your story out of the share list.There's also an optional white on black launcher icon. The settings got a cleaner layout with folding sections, and a clone install no longer crashes when the regular Messenger is on the same phone.

You'll need Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer.

### New in this release

- **Log out** is back. It's a row on the App page of the HushMessenger settings, and tapping it signs you out of the account on this phone the same way Messenger's own Log out does. You end up on Messenger's login screen, ready for the same account or a different one. There's no extra "are you sure" step. If a Messenger build ever moves its Log out, the row says so and points you to the one in Messenger's menu. Refs #88.
- **Square profile pictures** is a new switch under Theme, and it starts off. After a restart, profile pictures in the chat list, the stories row, chat headers and suggestions turn into squares, or rounded squares if you also turn on **Round the corners**. People who are online, the ones with the green dot, keep the same size as everyone else in the stories row. Notification pictures stay round. Refs #89.
- **Custom launcher icon** is a new patch that starts unselected. It turns Messenger's home screen icon white on black, or black on white if you pick that style, using Messenger's own logo. Themed icons on Android 13 and up still work. Patch again without it to get the normal icon back. Refs #107.
- HushMessenger's settings speak Traditional Chinese when your phone is set to it, in Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macau. Simplified Chinese still shows English for now. Thanks to @JhouHank for the translation. Refs #98.
- **Hide Your story when sharing** is a new switch under Photos and videos, and it starts off. Share a photo, video or link into Messenger from another app and the Send to list won't offer Your story anymore, so a stray tap on Add can't post it. Your chats and groups stay right where they were, and the story itself works as usual. Refs #102.

### Fixes and changes

- HushMessenger now targets Messenger 584.1.0.61.98 and takes all 21 builds APKMirror lists for it, arm64 and armv7 alike, including the three arm64 bundles `346817008`, `346817025` and `346817026`. 584.0.0.49.98 is no longer supported, so update Messenger before you patch. Each build was checked patch by patch, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt every one of them. Refs #106.
- Patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.0.1, which uses less memory while patching. You'll need Morphe Manager 2.2.0 or newer, or Morphe Desktop 1.19.1.
- The HushMessenger settings got a tighter layout, modeled on HushFacebook's. Every section folds up under its own header and starts closed, so the whole list fits on a couple of screens. Open the ones you use and they stay open next time. Searching still finds any control, whether its section is open or not. The banner with "Make Messenger yours" and the Inbox, Chats and More chips are gone. The colors now follow Messenger's own blue in both the light and dark theme, and Restart Messenger sits at the top of the App tab.
- Every HushMessenger title (the settings name, the sheet titles and the restart screen) now shows Messenger's blue to purple to pink to orange colors. They drift slowly with a light sheen now and then, and they keep moving even with Android's animations turned off.
- TalkBack reads each settings section's open or closed state once now. It used to say it twice, like "collapsed, Collapsed, Inbox".
- With large text, the little arrow on each settings section shows whole again. At 200% it was cut down to a sliver.
- **Source and licenses** under About opens the README's Credits section again. It pointed at a heading the README no longer has, so it landed at the top of the page.
- With **Open your gallery app** on and no default gallery set, the list Android shows you now holds only your gallery apps. It could slip in other pickers, like Contacts. Whichever gallery you tap still opens with your photos and videos together. Refs #94.
- If Messenger crashed in the last three days, **Report a problem** now adds a line saying where in the code it happened. It's only the names of the failing code, never the error text, so no file names or chat content go in. Refs #103.
- Checking what you picked from your gallery no longer holds up Messenger's screen. If you cancel, or the pick times out or loses its permission, you're back in the chat with nothing attached. Report a problem now notes how the last gallery pick ended, without any file names. Refs #94.
- The patch log now shows when each search through Messenger's code starts and finishes. The Wi-Fi search is faster and lighter on memory too, since it reads Messenger's code directly instead of building text for every reference it passes. Refs #93, #99, #100.
- In **Auto reply**, a picture always lands on the card you picked it for, and it's always the one you picked last. Before, a slow copy of an earlier pick could finish late and replace the newer picture, or put one back after you tapped Clear. Save waits while a picture is still copying.
- Picking a picture for an auto reply is safer with huge or slow files. HushMessenger reads the file once into its own copy, turns away files over 32 MB or 64 megapixels, and gives up after 30 seconds, then tells you which of those happened. Picking again or tapping Clear stops the earlier copy right away, and the picture you had before stays put.
- Some APKMirror downloads of Messenger only carry icons for one small screen size, so on a sharper phone the launcher icon and the icons in Messenger's settings look blurry and jagged. HushMessenger's settings now say so under About when your download is one of those, and the README lists which builds have icons for every screen. Patching a `nodpi` build fixes it. Refs #91.
- **Hide Meta AI** now reaches the search screen too. Tap the search bar and the box at the top used to say "Ask Meta AI or search" even with the switch on. Now it shows the plain search hint, like the bar on the Chats list. Search still finds people and chats the same way.
- **Clone install under another package name** no longer crashes a few seconds after you open the copy when the regular Messenger is on the phone too. The copy was saving its muted chats into the other Messenger's storage, which Android blocks, so now it keeps them in its own.
- With **Slide chats in and out** on, a chat whose first frames come late no longer jumps partway in. That happened most on the first chat you open after starting Messenger. The chat now waits off screen until Messenger draws on time (a quarter second at most), then slides in from the edge. Going back works the same way.

### Behind the scenes

- The install check now names the kind of refusal it finds and what to do about it. A Messenger signed with another key says which Android user it's installed for, so a copy hiding in Secure Folder or a work profile is easy to find. A permission held by another app (`INSTALL_FAILED_DUPLICATE_PERMISSION`) is no longer mixed up with a Messenger signer problem.
- The README's settings screenshots are new, and they now show the App tab too. They're rendered from the settings code, with a small record of which switches they show and each image's checksum. A release stops when a switch was added, renamed or retired since then, or when an image no longer matches. Any link from the app into the README has to reach a heading that exists.
- When another app takes the phone's screen in the middle of a walk, the failed step now says which app it was, instead of only saying it left no screen dump.
- The whole-app walk now has to show every screen it opened. Counting them is no longer enough. Each required step (a chat, both settings tabs, the message log and auto reply sheets when those patches are in, and each native screen) saves a screenshot and a UI dump next to the receipt, with their checksums. Publish reads those files again and refuses the walk when a step is missing or listed twice, a file is missing or changed, a screen shows the Restore or login prompt, two steps landed on the same screen, or a step ended up somewhere it shouldn't. An older receipt that only counted screens doesn't count anymore.
- Every Messenger screen in the walk now has to land on its own page. Any Messenger screen no longer passes. Each step checks the page it lands on and a label only that page has, so a link that drops back to the inbox fails. Messenger 584.1 ignores most of its old links when another app sends them (the inbox, Active now, stories, new message, stickers and Marketplace). The walk now opens the inbox from Messenger's own launcher and adds the story and contact settings pages, which still open by link.
- On Android 12 and older the walk can now pass the message log. Before Android 13 the log blocks screenshots to keep chat text out of Recents, so that one step keeps a record showing its window is locked instead. Every other step still needs its screenshot.

### Reports this release changed something for

#88 Log out, #89 square profile pictures, #94 gallery app list, #98 Traditional Chinese, #102 Your story in the share list, #103 crash details in Report a problem, #106 Messenger 584.1, #107 launcher icon, and #91, #93, #99 and #100.

Full history is in the [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

### How to update

1. Update Messenger to 584.1.0.61.98 first. 584.0 won't patch with this release. Any build on [APKMirror's 584.1.0.61.98 page](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/facebook-2/messenger/facebook-messenger-584-1-0-61-98-release/) works, and a `nodpi` one keeps the icons sharp.
2. In Morphe Manager, open **Sources** and refresh HushMessenger. The card should say **66 patches**.
3. Patch Messenger again and install it over your current one. Your settings carry over.

Patching on a computer? `patches-0.27.0.mpp` below is the same bundle for Morphe Desktop 1.19.1 or newer. It's a patch bundle, not a Messenger APK. `SHA256SUMS.txt` and its signature let you check the download, and the README says how.

### What was checked

- The full test suite, plus a patch run against every Messenger 584.1 build on file.
- Morphe Desktop patched and rebuilt one APK from each of the four build families.
- An APK patched from this exact bundle was installed on a Galaxy S22 over a signed-in Messenger. The chat, inbox, both HushMessenger settings tabs, the message log, auto reply and Messenger's own settings, story and contact pages all opened, with no crashes.
